text:
B: Hiya! Can you hear me alright? I'm Yusuf.
A: Yeah, I can hear you. Tracey.
B: Tracey, nice one. Where you calling from, Tracey?
A: Dagenham.
B: East London, nice. I'm Birmingham. Jewellery Quarter. So what do you do?
A: I'm a kitchen assistant. Primary school canteen. Is that what you wanted?
B: Yeah, no, that's perfect. What's that like, then? Day to day?
A: Erm, busy. I do the veg prep first thing, then I'm on the hatch at dinner time serving, then washing up and the clean at the end. Twenty-five hours, term-time. It's alright. My back don't love it but it's alright.
B: Proper graft, that. I couldn't do it. I'm an exec assistant for two directors at a property firm, so I'm sat at a desk all day doing their diaries. Honestly, if I'm off for one day, the whole office falls apart. They can't find a meeting room without me.
A: No, that's not right. Nobody's that important. Sorry, but it's not. They'd manage.
B: Ha! Okay, okay, fair. They'd manage. Badly, but they'd manage.
A: Our place had a cook who thought she was that important. She wasn't.
B: What happened with her?
A: Cutting corners. Reheating stuff she shouldn't. I said something to the manager and we fell out over it. I worried about it after, mind, but I'd do it again. It's kids' food, you know.
B: No, you're dead right. You can't mess about with that. Respect for saying something.
A: Mm.
B: So, what's on the menu at school then? What's the kids' favourite?
A: Jacket potatoes, and we ran out again Tuesday. Every week they don't order enough and I get the moaning at the hatch, not them in the office.
B: Always the person at the front who gets it. Same with me when a booking goes wrong. I just smooth it over, say the restaurant messed up.
A: Did they?
B: Erm. Sometimes.
A: Right.
B: I'll take that. You're the second person today who's caught me out, to be fair. Gemma, the teacher, she's got me on pie barms. Pie in a bread roll. Have you heard of that?
A: No, but I'd have it. I like pie and mash, there's a shop in Barking I go to. Proper, with liquor.
B: The green stuff? I've seen it on telly. I'd try it. I'm halal so I'd have to check the pie, but I'm game.
A: They do a veggie one now I think. Not the same though.
B: Got any holidays coming up?
A: Spain if we can afford it. All-inclusive, a week. I don't like the airport but once I'm there I'm fine. Steve, my husband, he does all the passports and that cos I get in a state.
B: Fair play to Steve. Where's the furthest you've been?
A: Turkey. I don't want to go anywhere too far or too foreign, I'm happy with what I know.
B: I'm the opposite, I always want somewhere new. Marrakech last year.
A: Each to their own. You look like you'd like all that. Your flat looks very smart.
B: Ah, thank you. Chloe does most of it, I just buy the trainers.
